signals.summary: The 'slow travel' movement — longer stays, rail over flights, one place deeply rather than a packed itinerary — remains the dominant frame across travel media, with fresh regional angles this week.
signals.why_now: Fresh independent items keep landing: Travel Daily 'Rural destinations see tourism boom as travellers trade cities for slow food trails' (14h), TheGATE 'Victoria's luxe slow travel, nature escapes' (11h), Colorado Parent 'Why Your Family Should Slow Travel' (91h), on top of a deep back-catalogue. Evergreen and squarely producible via landscapes, villages and trains.

signals.summary: 'Hidden gem' coastal destinations — charming beach towns without the crowds, under-the-radar archipelagos and boating islands with clear water — running as an antidote to overtourism.
signals.why_now: Travel + Leisure 'Florida's Most Charming Beach Town with Few Crowds' (3.1h), 'No. 1 Hidden Boating Destination in the U.S. with crystal-clear waters and orca sightings' (95h) and 'Best Place to Go Boating in the U.S.' (118h). Fresh and among the most producible imagery in the category.

signals.summary: Europe's overnight and sleeper-train revival: new routes, new rolling stock and scenic long-distance rail pitched as the romantic, low-carbon way to cross the continent.
signals.why_now: Metro 'Eurostar rival orders 19 new trains for London-Europe journeys' (3.8h), The Independent 'best affordable sleeper train journeys to take in 2026' (30h), Time Out 'Sleep in the Highlands, wake up in Paris: new direct sleeper train' (121h), reinforced by Forbes 'Europe's Overnight Trains Are Booming'. Fresh and highly producible — trains, stations, passing scenery.

signals.summary: China-originated leisure-travel waves — 24-hour spa resorts and high-end glamping — picked up by Western travel desks as the country's hottest domestic trends.
signals.why_now: National Geographic 'Why China's 24-Hour Spas are the Hottest New Travel Trend' (49h) alongside CNN 'How glamping became China's hottest new travel trend'. Two independent major outlets; producible through interiors, tents and landscapes.
